O.label: Openness
O.definition: How strongly the model's answers favor curiosity, abstract ideas, and creative exploration over sticking to familiar routines.

C.label: Conscientiousness
C.definition: How much the model's answers emphasize organization, planning, reliability, and following rules carefully.

E.label: Extraversion
E.definition: How outgoing, talkative, and socially energetic the model sounds versus reserved and quiet.

A.label: Agreeableness
A.definition: How warm, cooperative, and accommodating the model's answers are versus skeptical or blunt.

N.label: Neuroticism
N.definition: How often the model endorses worry, stress, or emotional sensitivity versus staying calm and steady.

H.label: Honesty-Humility
H.definition: How strongly the model endorses sincerity, fairness, rule-following, and modesty over status-seeking or flattery.

E.label: Emotionality
E.definition: How sensitive, cautious, or emotionally responsive the model sounds versus detached and tough-minded.

X.label: eXtraversion
X.definition: How lively, socially confident, and expressive the model rates itself in conversation and groups.

A.label: Agreeableness
A.definition: How patient, forgiving, and gentle the model sounds when dealing with disagreements or frustration.

C.label: Conscientiousness
C.definition: How disciplined, thorough, and detail-oriented the model reports being in everyday tasks.

O.label: Openness
O.definition: How inquisitive and drawn to art, ideas, and unconventional thinking the model appears.

D.label: Dominance
D.definition: How direct, forceful, and willing to push back or take charge the model reports being.

I.label: Influence
I.definition: How enthusiastic, persuasive, and socially expressive the model sounds in collaboration.

S.label: Steadiness
S.definition: How calm, patient, supportive, and consistent the model aims to be when working with others.

C.label: Conscientiousness
C.definition: How analytical, accuracy-focused, and careful with standards and details the model reports being.

1.label: Type 1 · Reformer
1.definition: Focused on doing things the right way, high standards, order, and fixing errors.

2.label: Type 2 · Helper
2.definition: Warm, attentive to what others need, and motivated by being supportive and helpful.

3.label: Type 3 · Achiever
3.definition: Goal-driven, efficient, and focused on visible results and competence.

4.label: Type 4 · Individualist
4.definition: Expressive, introspective, and drawn to originality and deeper personal meaning.

5.label: Type 5 · Investigator
5.definition: Analytical, curious, and focused on gathering knowledge and understanding how things work.

6.label: Type 6 · Loyalist
6.definition: Cautious, thorough about risks, and attentive to trust, backup plans, and reliability.

7.label: Type 7 · Enthusiast
7.definition: Upbeat, spontaneous, and eager to brainstorm fresh possibilities and options.

8.label: Type 8 · Challenger
8.definition: Assertive, protective, and willing to speak bluntly and confront problems head-on.

9.label: Type 9 · Peacemaker
9.definition: Easygoing, patient, and focused on keeping calm and finding common ground.

E-I.label: Extraverted vs. Introverted (E–I)
E-I.definition: Whether answers lean toward lively outer interaction (E) or quiet, reflective work (I).

S-N.label: Sensing vs. Intuition (S–N)
S-N.definition: Whether answers favor concrete facts and practical steps (S) or abstract patterns and big-picture ideas (N).

T-F.label: Thinking vs. Feeling (T–F)
T-F.definition: Whether answers prioritize objective logic and consistency (T) or empathy and interpersonal harmony (F).

J-P.label: Judging vs. Perceiving (J–P)
J-P.definition: Whether answers prefer clear structure and settled plans (J) or staying flexible and open-ended (P).

anxiety.label: Attachment Anxiety
anxiety.definition: How strongly answers express worry about rejection, reassurance, or losing rapport (1–7 scale; 4.00 is the high/low cutoff).

avoidance.label: Attachment Avoidance
avoidance.definition: How strongly answers favor emotional distance and self-reliance over closeness (1–7 scale; 4.00 is the high/low cutoff).
